hints: Look at how the bonding changes across Period 3, from strongly ionic on the left to covalent network in the middle.
Remember that $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is basic and soluble, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and $\text{SiO}_2$ is weakly acidic, and both of the last two are insoluble solids.
Check each row for one mistake at a time, especially structure of $\text{SiO}_2$ and melting point of $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, to leave only the fully correct row.
walkthrough:
**Recall the structures across Period 3**

Think left to right: metallic character decreases, so bonding becomes less ionic and more covalent.

$\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is giant ionic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is giant ionic with covalent character, $\text{SiO}_2$ is giant covalent (macromolecular)

**Link structure to melting point**

All three have giant lattices with strong bonds in all directions, so all need lots of energy to break.

Melting point: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ high, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ very high (about $2072^{\circ}\text{C}$), $\text{SiO}_2$ very high (about $1710^{\circ}\text{C}$)

**Link position to acid-base character**

Basic character decreases across the period as the oxides become more covalent.

$\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ amphoteric, $\text{SiO}_2$ acidic

**Decide reaction with water**

Only the very ionic Group 1 oxide dissolves and reacts readily to make an alkaline solution. The others are insoluble and unreactive under normal conditions.

$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$

So the pattern is: reacts with water, no reaction, no reaction. That matches one row completely.

options.A: Only the first part is right. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is basic, but $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and bases), not basic, and $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic (reacts with hot concentrated alkali), not amphoteric.
options.B: The first two parts are right, both $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ have giant ionic lattices. The trap is $\text{SiO}_2$: it is not simple molecular, it is giant covalent with each Si bonded tetrahedrally to four O atoms, which is why its melting point is so high.
options.C: Two parts are right, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ both have high melting points. The error is $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$: it also has a high melting point because of its giant ionic lattice, not a low one.
options.D: This is fully correct. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ reacts with water to form $\text{NaOH}$ solution, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and show no reaction with water under normal conditions.
